info.name: Elevateo Mail API
info.description: Generated from the canonical Elevateo contracts (v1 session/mailbox API and v2 additive API). Requests authenticate with the browser session cookie: sign in to the same host first, then fill sessionContext and authorizationVersion from GET /v1/session. No credential is stored in this collection.

item.name: v1 · Elevateo local session and mailbox contract (1.0.0-organization-threads.1)
item.description: Canonical accepted BE-02A lifecycle amendment and unchanged FE-01 read checkpoint. Design contract, not implementation acceptance. All mail content is plaintext. See README.md for normative authorization, lifecycle, byte limits and transport rules.

request.description: Authenticate and check current session revocation before returning actor, organization, context and in-memory CSRF bootstrap token. Does not create or refresh a login. Does not list mailboxes; getMailboxes is the sole capability list. A valid cookie with no currently usable organization returns not_available.

request.description: Current-authorized conversation in the explicitly selected mailbox; mismatched mailbox and thread is not_available. Messages have independent keyset pagination by sent_at ascending, null first, then id ascending. Cursor binds thread and mailbox plus actor, organization, session context, authorization version, ordering and limit. Empty conversations are valid. Does not mark read.
Issue a five-minute signed browser challenge without calling Auth. Bind to both current session digest and pending-entry digest when present. No query parameters; no identity or account information.

request.description: Exact Origin plus challenge bound to the pending entry. Claim the entry before POST verify, then set password and verify identity before publishing a local session. Pending entry grants no mail access. Replayed/expired/ambiguous verification fails generically; known password_pending state may retry only password setting, never blindly retry the one-time hash. Clear pending-entry and challenge cookies on completion.

request.description: Exact Origin and challenge bound to the existing opaque session. A locally valid cookie with an expired access JWT may refresh; do not require the ordinary online-read precheck. Commit one durable claim, call Auth once, and CAS publish within the original ten-second request deadline. Contenders return 503 Retry-After 1. Uncertain/expired claim requires reauthentication; never steal/replay it or resurrect after logout. Context and CSRF remain stable. With no selected organization, explicit refresh may select a newly provisioned membership; otherwise keep the local cookie and return 404.

request.description: Exact Origin and current session CSRF or challenge bound to the supplied cookie. Commit local/default or all bound-user local/global revocation and durable upstream intent before Auth. Clear cookie even if Auth is down or access JWT expired. Missing/invalid cookie with valid challenge is idempotent local completion without identity data. Never accept a browser user ID. Clear session and challenge cookies. Global scope requires a locally valid bound user; an expired local session cannot perform global logout and returns 401.

request.description: Complete durable save with current compose permission and session/context/Origin/CSRF. expected_version=0 creates version 1; positive expected_version must equal current version. After current scope/ownership checks, inspect the actor/org/operation unique ledger before draft version/state or reply-target checks: same binding and canonical digest returns the original applied result even after later save B or consumption; a recorded conflict replays its original 409. Different binding/digest or any expired ID gives 409 operation_mismatch. For a new operation, reply_to_thread_id must be null or a currently readable thread in this mailbox; consumed drafts give draft_consumed, then stale/missing versions give draft_conflict. No live send or consume endpoint. Save and terminal ledger record commit atomically; concurrent identical requests converge without incrementing twice. See docs/completion/be02-cd-contract.md for the exact digest and seven-day retention boundary.

request.description: Authorize current session/context, compose capability, requested draft ownership and mailbox scope before ledger lookup. An unclaimed/absent own-draft ID in an authorized mailbox may return unknown for an in-flight creation; an existing foreign/hidden draft is generic 404. Lookup uses only the current actor/org key, never another actor's ledger. A known own operation with a different requested mailbox/draft binding is generic 404. Applied/conflict returns original metadata only, even after later saves; no body/recipients/subject/digest. At recorded_at + seven days or later return expired even if physical compaction is delayed. Absence is unknown, never not performed. GET cannot execute, reserve or retry a save.

request.description: Any current mailbox reader may set only their own thread read boolean. No actor supplied by the caller. Missing state defaults unread; matching desired state is a no-op. Differing writes serialize and last committed wins; returned revision is informational, not a precondition. Unchanged B GET unread is exactly the inverse of this persisted boolean, defaults true; GET never changes it. New inbound-message behavior is outside BE-02.

Matching desired state is a no-op.

First create returns 201; same current actor, mailbox, thread, note_id and exact body returns original note with 200. Same actor's currently visible existing ID with different binding/content returns 409 operation_mismatch; another author's or hidden ID is generic 404. Current authorization precedes replay. No edit/delete route, note notification or implicit email send.

request.description: Current manage_members required; path target must be a current member of this organization, otherwise generic 404. Compare expected_membership_version to mailbox-wide revision; stale revision or demoting the final current manager returns 409 membership_conflict. Upsert the explicit reader row and replace all three flags; identical existing flags at current version is a no-op. Every stored membership change increments mailbox revision and affected authorization generations atomically under session, sorted generation and mailbox/business guards, even when shared read already existed; never direct membership-table grants. Provisioning is separate.

request.description: Current manage_members required; target must currently belong to this organization. expected_membership_version is a required single query integer; DELETE has no body. Stale mailbox revision or removal of the final current manager returns 409 membership_conflict. At the matching revision an absent explicit row is a no-op with member=null; an existing row is removed and mailbox revision/affected authorization generations increment atomically. Shared organization readers can retain read after explicit removal. Re-bootstrap after a successful permission change; no late response restores prior authority.

request.description: Search only currently authorized plaintext thread subject and message body/sender/to display names and addresses; never drafts or notes. q is 1..256 Unicode code points, not solely whitespace, and otherwise preserved. Literal case-insensitive substring matching using parameterized PostgreSQL with %, _ and backslash escaped as literals; no SQL/regex/tsquery syntax from callers. Match a thread once if any authorized searchable field contains q; return its unchanged canonical ThreadSummary preview, not an HTML highlight or an extra excerpt. Optional mailbox must be currently readable or generic 404. Order last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC; at most 50/256 KiB, signed scoped cursor, whole entries, no totals. Existing database query only; indexes need representative EXPLAIN evidence. Search never returns threads in the spam or trash folders.

request.description: List threads across every mailbox currently readable by the authenticated actor in the active organization. One authorized repeatable-read snapshot; each mailbox contributes at most limit+1 candidates to the global keyset merge. Order last_message_at descending, null last, then id descending. Cursor binds actor, organization, session context, authorization version, filter, ordering and limit, and cannot be used with a mailbox list. Concurrent activity may move threads ahead of a continuation; refresh to see them. No totals and no read-state mutation.
